primary_title: STAT3 targets the regulatory regions of gluconeogenic genes in vivo
decision_basis: Review-guided primary evidence identifies G6PC/G6Pase as a STAT3-bound hepatic regulatory target whose expression is repressed by IL-6-activated STAT3.
limitations_preserved: STAT3 promoter occupancy, IL-6-dependent repression and reduced RNA polymerase II/histone acetylation support G6PC gene repression; preserve hepatic metabolic context and do not infer reduced G6PC protein or a CNS/SCI effect automatically.

primary_title: STAT3 targets the regulatory regions of gluconeogenic genes in vivo
decision_basis: Review-guided primary evidence identifies PCK1/PEPCK as a STAT3-bound hepatic regulatory target repressed by STAT3, with regulation detectable independently of IL-6 activation.
limitations_preserved: STAT3 promoter occupancy and STAT3-dependent PCK1 repression support gene-level regulation; preserve the basal-versus-IL-6 and hepatic context and do not infer PCK1 protein, metabolic flux or CNS/SCI effects automatically.

primary_title: FAP Promotes Immunosuppression by Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts in the Tumor Microenvironment via STAT3-CCL2 Signaling
decision_basis: Review-guided primary evidence identifies a FAP-positive cancer-associated-fibroblast STAT3–CCL2 axis with STAT3 occupancy at the CCL2 regulatory region and STAT3-dependent CCL2 expression.
limitations_preserved: STAT3 occupancy and perturbation-supported CCL2 expression establish a bounded CAF gene-level activation edge; preserve FAP/uPAR/FAK-Src-JAK2 and tumor context, and do not equate CCL2 gene transcription with secreted protein in every state or infer SCI.

primary_title: STAT5 programs a distinct subset of GM-CSF-producing T helper cells that is essential for autoimmune neuroinflammation
decision_basis: Review-guided primary evidence identifies IL-7-activated STAT5 as a direct Csf2 promoter-binding regulator of GM-CSF production in pathogenic CD4-positive T helper cells.
limitations_preserved: STAT5 promoter occupancy, Stat5 loss-of-function and Csf2 expression/protein readouts support gene-level activation with an EAE-relevant T-cell context; preserve the transcription-to-cytokine-production distinction and do not treat gene activation as automatic secretion or infer a terminal TF.
